Child care subsidies in Comox Valley

What Comox Valley families actually pay after CCFRI, the Affordable Child Care Benefit and $10-a-day — and how to claim each one.

Child care in Comox Valley, BC costs far less than the sticker price once subsidies are applied. Comox Valley families have access to the same three BC programs as everyone in the province — here's how each one works, what you'll actually pay, and how to claim them.

🧾
automatic

CCFRI fee reduction

Your centre opts in and the reduction lands on your invoice automatically — no application, no income test. Up to $900/month for under-3s.

💸
income-tested

Affordable Child Care Benefit

You apply and renew yearly; household income up to ~$111,000 qualifies. Stacks on top of CCFRI — for lower incomes it can reach close to $0.

🔟
at $10/day sites

$10-a-day (CWELCC)

At participating Comox Valley sites, full-time fees are capped at about $200/month ($10/day).

How Comox Valley families apply

  1. CCFRI — nothing to do. Ask your Comox Valley centre if they're a CCFRI participant (most are); the reduction shows on your invoice.
  2. Affordable Child Care Benefit — apply online via My Family Services, with your SIN, CRA Notice of Assessment, your child's birth certificate and banking details. Full walkthrough: how to apply for the ACCB.
  3. Complete the CF2798 with your provider — our free CF2798 helper fills most of it for you.
  4. Renew every year so your reduction doesn't lapse.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the child care subsidy in Comox Valley?
Comox Valley families get the same BC subsidies as the rest of the province. At a participating centre, CCFRI lowers fees automatically — up to $900/month for infants and toddlers and $545 for 3-years-to-Kindergarten (group rates). The income-tested Affordable Child Care Benefit (household income up to about $111,000) can reduce your fee further, and $10-a-day sites cap full-time fees at roughly $200/month.
Do Comox Valley daycares offer CCFRI and $10-a-day?
Most licensed Comox Valley centres take part in CCFRI, and a growing number are $10-a-day (CWELCC) sites. Check each centre on our Comox Valley childcare board or ask the centre directly.
How do I apply for child care subsidy in Comox Valley?
CCFRI is automatic at a participating centre — there's nothing to apply for. For the Affordable Child Care Benefit you apply through My Family Services and submit a CF2798 Child Care Arrangement form with your provider — see our step-by-step guide.
